data.description:
Granola is the AI notepad for people in back-to-back meetings. We're growing fast and looking for a hands-on affiliate / influencer / creator marketer to help us scale our partnership programmes across evergreen and launch campaigns. This is an individual contributor role.

The opportunity

We are looking for an affiliate and influencer marketer to join our team at Granola. We work with hundreds of creators and publishers to support acquiring new users through partnerships (sponsorships, affiliation and hybrid models).

You'll sit at the intersection of branding and growth, making sure we’re proud of the online narratives around Granola and checking the performance of our influencer marketing efforts at a channel and partner level.

What you’ll do

  • Own a creator portfolio : Be responsible for growing and looking after a large portfolio of key accounts (sponsored, affiliates or hybrid) and regularly keeping in touch with them to increase Granola’s presence on their different channels

  • Newsletter sponsorships : You'll own this channel end to end, from partner onboarding and booking through live-date tracking, invoicing, and performance reporting.

  • Influencer partnerships : Sourcing and onboarding great creators for authentic collaborations. Instead of an ad placement, you’ll do demos of granola, find ideas and creative briefs for the influencers that would bring new user acquisitions too

  • YouTube collaborations : Running campaigns with youtube creators to meet internal priorities through integrations, dedicated videos and editorial projects.

Example projects you might work on

  • Newsletter creatives : draft launch announcements and evergreen copy, and work with our design and copywriting team to get assets for our ads placements. Review editorial pieces for accuracy and brand safety.

  • AEO portfolio. Increase the amount of citations on LLM through YouTube partnerships and listicle sponsorships, measuring the impact on citations from your work

  • Account management : being the point of contact for a portfolio of affiliates / creators with large audiences, building win-win deals and generating authentic content.

Your background looks something like…

  • 3 years in influencer / affiliate marketing, brand-side or agency side. You’ve worked on significant creator collaborations that had tangible business impact (we’ll ask for example of campaigns you’ve run or a portfolio)

  • A track record of managing a large portfolio of accounts and co-building the systems to support working with hundreds of vendors and deals at once, without sacrificing the quality of deliverables

  • Experience working at a startup or scale up, preferably in tech, AI or B2B SaaS space. You understand the future of work and Granola’s ICP (enterprise and self-serve)

As a person, you…

  • Have high-agency and business acumen. You’re able to autonomously allocate budget, negotiate with creators, unstuck collaborations including at-risk accounts

  • Are AI-native but know when to use it and when it is an overkill

  • Are extremely good at prioritizing - picking what will really move the needles with goals and saying no to what is just busy work

  • Have deep interest, curiosity and understanding around the creator economy and brand partnerships. You know that the playbooks get constantly re-written and you proactively keep up with the industry.

  • Are chronically online and already know partners that would be a great fit for Granola. Bonus if you have existing relationships with creators, publishers and key opinion leaders that would be a great fit for Granola.

  • Are creative and can select creators who have a tasteful editorial line and content style. You’d be able to scout the partners we’d be proud to collaborate with not only through data but also by instincts. Your experience helps you tell who can build trust and influence.

About the opportunity

This is the opportunity to come shape the narrative of Granola with creators while generating measurable growth, on the branding and user acquisition side, and create business impact at one of the fastest growing AI company in London.

We work primarily together in London (office-first). You can find more about the team, how we work and our benefits on our careers page.

If this sounds like work you’d love doing, we’d like to hear from you—even if your experience doesn’t match every point above.

Compensation

Our compensation philosophy is to hire the best people in the market and pay them accordingly with salary, variable, and equity.

About Zego 🚀

At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.

Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive.

We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖

For us, AI isn't a line on a roadmap or a buzzword on a slide. It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook.

We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers.

Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor.

If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring.

What you'll be doing

  • You will work through the new and existing business leads by making outbound calls to prospective customers, helping them through the sales process.

We are the creators of Flipper Zero — a portable device for tech enthusiasts and engineers. It’s a gadget with an awesome community that brings together millions of people around the world.

We’re building a new product — Flipper One. It’s a full-featured ARM-based computer running Linux in a compact form factor, powered by the Rockchip RK3576 SoC.

We’ve decided to make the entire development process completely open and public. That’s why we’re looking for a Developer Portal & Community Manager to own and manage the entire Flipper One Developer Portal: maintaining the wiki, collecting tasks from all development teams, managing all GitHub projects and repositories, and proactively communicating with the community.

This role is perfect for you if you want to be close to the product, see firsthand how it’s built, and help turn that process into a clear and valuable entry point for the community. This is not a “content manager” role — you’ll need to fully understand the development process, track all ongoing tasks, and connect the team with the community to make things happen.

What is the Developer Portal?

The Developer Portal is a public wiki + a set of GitHub projects built around Flipper One. It documents how the project works as a whole, explains the architecture of its major subsystems, and provides contribution guides for the community — showing how people can contribute to each sub-project.

Anyone reading the Developer Portal wiki should come away with a complete understanding of the project structure, each feature, and what exactly we are building.

Requirements:

  • You write clearly, concisely, and without fluff, and can show examples of your work: guides, instructions, READMEs, how-tos, or similar materials

  • Basic understanding of hardware, software, and development workflows (Git, commits, branches, pull requests)

  • Able to explain complex technical topics in simple language and visualize them with flowchart sketches

  • Strong verbal communication skills; you know how to listen, ask precise questions, and quickly extract the key points from chaotic discussions

  • Keep communication with the community productive — without toxicity, unnecessary softness, or bureaucracy

  • Comfortable collaborating closely with engineers and navigating technical contexts

  • Discern useful feedback and constructive disagreement from noise and spam

  • Value structure, logic, clarity, and information quality

  • Genuinely interested in developer-facing products, hardware, documentation, open communities, and the build-in-public approach

  • Proficiency in Russian and English for communication with other departments in the company and the external community

Nice-to-have:

  • Experience in DevRel, technical writing, community operations, or an editorial role

  • Experience working with documentation, wikis, knowledge bases, or developer portals

  • Understanding of the culture of technical communities, open-source, and hardware projects

  • Ability to work across topics at the intersection of interfaces, electronics, product architecture, and internal development

Responsibilites:

  • Own and develop the Flipper One Developer Portal

  • Turn the team’s internal context into clear public documentation, notes, updates, and explanations

  • Join team calls to understand what’s actually happening in the project and maintain a complete picture of it

  • Translate technical discussions into clear, human language without losing meaning or accuracy

  • Moderate community comments, pull requests, and contributions

  • Filter out spam, reduce noise, and keep discussions productive

  • Help users understand how the portal works and how to provide useful feedback

  • Collect signals from the community and bring them back to the team

  • Make sure the portal stays structured, up to date, and genuinely useful

What we offer:

  • Fully remote from anywhere in the world

  • You will be provided with all the necessary equipment for a comfortable working environment

  • Benefits such as VHI, corporate sports, foreign language courses, and therapy sessions

About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

Based in the UK you will be a key member of the Manufacturing Operations team where you will drive the development of our business management systems as well as our product, supplier, software and customer quality initiatives.

You will be comfortable with assessing processes and technologies to identify quality gaps and provide robust but pragmatic solutions to drive all aspects of the business in achieving the highest levels of quality and resilience.

Key responsibilities

  • Define and deliver the company quality strategy, policy and objectives, aligned to the product roadmap and growth plan.

  • Build, lead and develop a quality team covering supplier, product, reliability, software and systems quality.

  • Define and report quality performance to the executive team.

  • Establish appropriate document control, change control, CAPA, internal audit, training and records processes that scale with a fast-growing fabless company.

  • Work with PMO to embed quality gates into the new product introduction (NPI) and product lifecycle process, from concept through end of life.

  • Own quality across the supply chain: wafer foundry, assembly and packaging, wafer and final test, PCB/PCBA and system-level contract manufacturers.

  • Lead supplier selection, qualification, audits and ongoing performance management, including scorecards and quarterly business reviews.

  • Work with engineering leaders to define software quality standards across drivers, firmware, compilers, SDKs and runtime.

  • Establish release criteria, test coverage expectations, defect management and regression processes, aligned with CI/CD practice.

  • Bring in secure development and software supply chain practice, including SBOMs and vulnerability management.

  • Support responsible AI and AI management practice where customers ask for it, including awareness of ISO/IEC 42001.

  • Be the senior point of contact for customer quality, audits and escalations.

  • Lead customer RMA and complaint handling, root cause analysis and 8D responses to agreed timelines.

  • Ensure product compliance with RoHS, REACH, WEEE, conflict minerals reporting, UKCA and CE marking, and relevant safety and EMC standards.

Essential experience and skills

  • Significant experience in quality roles in semiconductors or electronics hardware, including creating and leading a quality function or team.

  • Direct experience managing quality through outsourced manufacturing: foundries, OSATs, test houses and/or contract manufacturers.

  • Deep knowledge of ISO 9001 and hands-on experience building or running a certified QMS.

  • Working knowledge of semiconductor qualification and reliability (JEDEC), failure analysis and

  • Awareness of data centre RAS assessments and HPC system qualification and certification.

  • Fluency in core quality tools: 8D, FMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA and root cause analysis.

  • Experience handling customer quality escalations with large, demanding customers.

  • Degree in electrical or electronic engineering, materials science, physics or a related discipline.

  • Clear, confident communicator who can influence engineers, suppliers and executives, and hold partners to account.

  • Willing to travel internationally, including to Asia and US, for supplier audits and customer quality reviews.

Desirable

  • Experience in a fabless company, particularly one bringing an initial product to volume.

  • Background in high-performance compute, data centre, networking or AI hardware.

  • Exposure to software quality, release management or secure development practice.

  • Lead auditor certification (ISO 9001), Six Sigma Black Belt, or chartered status (for example CQI or IET).

  • Experience working with suppliers in Taiwan, South Korea or US.

The impact you will have

You will help Fractile to makes sure every one of our suppliers builds to our standard, and that our customers receive AI hardware and software they can trust in production whilst shaping the quality culture across engineering, operations and commercial teams.

  • Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role.

  • Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation.

  • Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance.

  • Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment.

Job title: Applied ML Technical Lead, Defence

Location: London; full in-office working as default

Start date: ASAP

Reports to: CEO

Compensation: Salary and Equity options available for discussion

Clearance: Must be eligible to hold UK Security Vetting Clearance SC or above (no prior clearance required)

Application Deadline: 08/11/26 at 23:59 UK Time

___________________________________________________________________________

Help put frontier AI to work in Defence

Cosine is a UK AI lab building models, applications and training infrastructure for mission-critical organisations.

We build coding agents that work across real software systems, specialised Lumen models, AI-native security products and the infrastructure needed to deploy advanced AI in demanding environments. Our customers include some of the world's largest enterprises, including organisations operating behind strict security, regulatory and technical constraints.

We're also training Lumen Sovereign, the first frontier large language model trained in the UK, with the support of the UK Government.

We're now looking for an Applied ML Technical Lead to help develop and deploy advanced AI capabilities for organisations operating in UK Defence and national security.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will work across machine learning development, deployment and customer-facing technical delivery. You may spend part of your time training and evaluating models on complex sensor data, and part of your time working with Defence stakeholders to understand operational needs, shape priorities and guide delivery.

You will not be expected to act as a traditional project manager. Instead, you will own the technical direction and day-to-day progress of applied ML work, coordinating the people and decisions needed to turn promising research into useful operational capability.

___________________________________________________________________________

What you'll do

  • Build ML capabilities for real Defence problems

  • Design, build, train and evaluate machine learning models for challenging applied Defence and national security use cases.

  • Work on problems involving complex sensor data, signal processing, pattern recognition, classification and multimodal intelligence.

  • Develop and improve model architectures, training pipelines, evaluation frameworks and inference systems.

  • Work with real-world and synthetic datasets to improve model accuracy, robustness and generalisation.

  • Translate research prototypes into reliable, deployable capabilities that operate within demanding technical and security constraints.

  • Work closely with Cosine's ML research and engineering teams while taking direct ownership of technical outcomes.

Lead technical delivery from prototype to deployment

  • Own the technical direction and day-to-day progress of applied ML projects.

  • Turn operational objectives into concrete technical goals, experiments, milestones and success measures.

  • Coordinate work across ML researchers, software engineers, infrastructure teams and external stakeholders.

  • Identify technical dependencies, delivery risks and blockers, and help drive them to resolution.

  • Establish clear evaluation criteria and demonstrate progress through measurable improvements and working capabilities.

  • Balance hands-on engineering with the planning and coordination needed to keep complex technical work moving.

Work directly with Defence customers

  • Engage with technical and operational stakeholders across the UK Defence and national security ecosystem.

  • Understand operational challenges and identify where machine learning can make a meaningful difference.

  • Translate customer requirements and constraints into technical objectives, datasets, experiments and delivery plans.

  • Present technical progress, demonstrate working capabilities and communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Build trusted relationships with Defence stakeholders and act as a credible technical counterpart.

  • Help customers understand the practical considerations of integrating and deploying ML systems in their existing environments.

Turn research into operational capability

  • Help deploy ML models into real-world environments, including secure, on-premise and resource-constrained systems.

  • Work on model optimisation, inference performance, integration and reliability.

  • Develop robust approaches to evaluation, validation and continuous model improvement.

  • Understand data availability, access requirements, security restrictions and deployment constraints.

  • Establish feedback loops between operational users and Cosine's engineering teams.

  • Ensure that what we build is not only technically impressive, but genuinely useful to the people relying on it.

___________________________________________________________________________

What we’re looking for

You'll probably have a background in applied machine learning, ML engineering, research engineering or a similarly technical role, along with experience taking ownership of complex technical work.

You should be comfortable:

  • Writing production-quality Python and working with modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch.

  • Building, training, fine-tuning and evaluating machine learning models.

  • Working with complex datasets, designing experiments and interpreting model performance.

  • Understanding the trade-offs between model performance, compute requirements, latency and deployment constraints.

  • Working with engineering infrastructure, including Git, containers, Linux and GPU compute.

  • Taking technical ownership of projects with multiple stakeholders, uncertain requirements and evolving priorities.

  • Communicating technical concepts clearly to researchers, engineers, senior stakeholders and operational users.

  • Moving between model development, customer discussions and delivery planning without losing technical depth.

  • Making sound technical judgements, prioritising effectively and finding practical solutions when the path forward is unclear.

  • You don't need to have worked in Defence before. You do need to be excited by the opportunity to apply advanced ML to difficult, consequential real-world problems.

Nice to have

  • Existing UK security clearance, such as SC or DV, or previous experience working in secure Defence environments.

  • Experience with signal processing, time-series data, sensor fusion, representation learning or machine learning applied to complex real-world datasets.

  • Experience with foundation models, multimodal learning or advanced model training and post-training techniques.

  • Experience deploying ML models to edge devices or constrained compute environments.

  • Familiarity with UK Defence procurement, technical assurance or the national security landscape.

  • Experience leading technical workstreams or working as a technical lead on customer-facing ML projects.

___________________________________________________________________________

What success looks like

In your first three months, we would expect you to:

  • Become the technical lead for a major applied Defence ML programme, with responsibility for its day-to-day technical progress.

  • Build strong working relationships with Cosine's ML researchers, engineers and key Defence customer stakeholders.

  • Develop a clear understanding of the existing models, datasets, technical architecture and operational objectives.

  • Establish a focused delivery plan with clear priorities, milestones, ownership and success measures.

  • Make meaningful hands-on contributions to model development, evaluation or deployment.

  • Identify and begin addressing the most important technical and operational blockers.

  • Demonstrate tangible progress to customer stakeholders and build confidence in Cosine's ability to deliver.

  • Longer term, you'll help take advanced ML capabilities from promising prototypes into operational use, while shaping how Cosine builds and delivers applied AI for Defence and other mission-critical organisations.

___________________________________________________________________________

Why this role matters

Some of the most important applications of AI won't be found in consumer products. They'll be in environments where information is incomplete, systems are complex, security matters and the consequences of getting things wrong are significant.

Cosine is working to bring frontier machine learning into those environments.

Doing that requires more than good models. It requires people who can understand an operational problem, build something that works, make good technical decisions, coordinate the work needed to deliver it and stay close to the customer until it creates real value.

You'll have unusual proximity to cutting-edge ML research, senior Defence stakeholders and the operational challenges that will shape the next generation of AI capabilities.

This role will suit someone who is technically strong enough to build, organised enough to lead technical delivery and curious enough to engage directly with the people using the technology.

If you enjoy being close to the research, close to customers and personally accountable for turning ambitious technology into something real, come and work with us.

Help train the software engineers of the future

Cosine is building autonomous software-engineering systems for organisations where reliability, security and control matter most.

Our Lumen Enterprise models are designed to work across real codebases. They need to understand unfamiliar architectures, make changes across multiple files, use tools, run tests and produce software that engineers can maintain and trust.

We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to help train and improve these models.

You’ll work across the full training stack, including pre-training, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. This is a truly unique role that will provide exposure across all areas of the model training lifecycle. WE’re looking for someone who is just as happy to profile the training loop, identifying performance bottlenecks and memory leaks, as implementing new RL algorithms.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working close to the model and cares about the quality of the software it produces.

The models you train will write code, use development tools, run tests and receive feedback from real software-engineering environments. Your work will directly influence how Lumen reasons about code, navigates unfamiliar systems and improves through experience.

The best coding models are not simply the ones that generate plausible code.

They need to understand context, respect existing architecture, use tools effectively, test their work and recover when their first attempt fails. They need to produce changes that work in the real world, not just on a benchmark.

That behaviour has to be trained.

You’ll work directly on the data, environments, rewards and evaluations that shape Lumen’s capabilities. Your work will influence the models used by engineers and enterprise teams working on complex and security-sensitive software systems.

About the role

Radiant exists to redefine how AI infrastructure is built and operated at scale. We are creating a vertically integrated AI platform that brings together physical infrastructure, control planes, and cloud-native software to deliver abundance, control, and sovereignty in a world constrained by traditional hyperscaler models.

Our vision is to enable organisations to build, train, and deploy AI at national and global scale without surrendering control over performance, cost, or locality. This requires engineering systems that operate across software, hardware, and physical environments, and that remain reliable as scale and complexity increase.

We are scaling our engineering organisation now. Most of our engineering manager seats are open. You join, shape how the teams work, and grow with them.

As an Engineering Manager, you lead a team building and operating core parts of Radiant's cloud platform. You combine people leadership, technical judgement, delivery ownership and cross-functional collaboration. You work closely with product, infrastructure, SRE, security and other engineering teams.

This is a hands-on leadership role. It focuses on building strong teams, delivering reliable platform capabilities, and creating an environment where engineers do their best work.

The streams

We run engineering as ten streams in three groups. Each stream is a full team of about nine people: principal, senior and mid-level software engineers, an SDET, a DevOps engineer and a platform engineer. Each stream has its own engineering manager.

  • Infrastructure: Compute, Network, Storage, Cluster

  • Platform: Cloud, Infra, Observability, Security

  • AI: Training, Inference

You do not apply for a single stream. We hire strong managers first. Then we agree your stream with you, based on your strengths and interests. Your first stream is a starting point, not a fixed track. Moves between streams are normal here.

Key responsibilities

You lead one stream end to end: people, delivery and production.

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of about nine engineers across platform, infrastructure and distributed systems.

  • Own team execution across planning, prioritisation, delivery, quality and operational readiness.

  • Partner with product to turn priorities into clear technical plans and achievable milestones.

  • Provide technical leadership on architecture, reliability, scalability and engineering trade-offs.

  • Set strong engineering practices for design, testing, observability, documentation and incident learning.

  • Improve team effectiveness through clear ownership, healthy processes and strong cross-team collaboration.

  • Hire, onboard and retain high-performing engineers. Hiring is a large part of the first year. Expect around two hours a day on it.

  • Support career development through regular feedback, coaching and progression planning.

  • Manage technical risk, dependencies and delivery challenges across complex platform initiatives.

  • Bring AI-assisted engineering into daily work, within our guardrails.

  • Build a culture of ownership, pragmatism, operational excellence and continuous improvement.

Attitude comes first

  • Curiosity: you learn new domains fast. GPUs, networks and storage excite you rather than worry you.

  • Candour: you say what you think, with care. You welcome challenge to your own ideas.

  • Builder mindset: much here is not built yet. You enjoy creating the process, not just running it.

  • Pace with standards: you move fast and keep quality high.

  • Generosity: you make the people around you better. You give credit and share what you know.

Your profile

  • Experience leading engineering teams building cloud platforms, infrastructure, developer tooling or distributed systems.

  • A strong technical background. You engage credibly in architecture and design discussions.

  • A good understanding of:

    • Cloud infrastructure: compute, storage, networking, Kubernetes, containers

    • Platform engineering: APIs, automation, IAM, observability, reliability

    • Distributed systems: scaling, consistency, failure handling

    • Engineering operations: incident response, capacity, performance, production ownership

  • Proven experience in people management, hiring, coaching and performance development.

  • Strong delivery and prioritisation skills across competing priorities.

  • Comfort working closely with product and other engineering leaders in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment.

  • The ability to balance technical quality, delivery speed, reliability and team sustainability.

Experience with GPU, HPC or AI infrastructure is a bonus. Nobody has depth in every area above. Tell us which you know and which you want to learn.

What you bring

  • People leadership: you build strong teams and help engineers grow.

  • Technical judgement: you challenge designs and guide trade-offs without owning every implementation detail.

  • Execution: you create clarity and drive complex work to completion.

  • Systems thinking: you understand how platform components and teams fit together.

  • Operational mindset: you care about reliability, maintainability and production quality.

  • Ownership: you take responsibility for both team health and engineering outcomes.

The Role

As an AI Deployment Lead / Applied AI Consultant, you'll work directly with our most strategic customers to understand their objectives and key challenges, identify high-impact AI opportunities, and translate them into measurable business value.

You'll be building AI solutions on Omnea's procurement automation platform, combining the structured data flowing through requests, approvals, contracts, and supplier records with AI. Omnea gives AI the operational context of how a business actually buys, so it can move past answering questions and start taking action inside procurement itself: routing requests, flagging risk, drafting contract terms, negotiating with suppliers. There is no AI without that context.

You'll prototype these solutions, demonstrate their value to executives, and ensure successful implementation, adoption, and value realisation, growing Omnea's footprint at those customers as you go.

This customer-facing role is ideal for people who enjoy working directly with customers and turning complex business challenges into practical AI solutions. The focus is on problem framing, solution design, and business impact rather than pure implementation. While you will prototype AI solutions, the primary goal is to deliver meaningful business value to customers.

What You'll Do

data.description:
Our Mission

At Omnea, we’re reinventing how enterprise businesses operate, starting with the most painful parts: procurement – where a single purchase can drag on for months, trigger 50+ emails, and pull in Finance, Legal, Security, and IT just to get something approved.

We’ve raised $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners, and Accel to change that. Our AI-native platform connects every person, step, and system so buying is fast, safe, and efficient – one place to request, automated approvals and renewals, real-time supplier risk, and complete spend visibility.

The opportunity is massive. Every enterprise on the planet has this problem and nobody has solved it. We’ve 10x’d ARR to double-digit millions in 18 months and are trusted by global enterprises like Spotify, MongoDB, Monzo, and Albertsons. We’re now the 4th fastest growing startup in Europe & the Sunday Times' #1 Best Medium Sized Tech Company To Work for.

Our team previously scaled Tessian (cybersecurity tech, backed by Sequoia, Balderton, Accel, acquired post-Series C), and our team includes ex-founders operators who’ve grown unicorns, shipped world-class products, and executed at the highest levels. You’ll work alongside leaders like Ben, Abs, Sabrina, and Rebe.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

The Role

AI is changing what it means to deploy enterprise software. Configuring a customer's procurement workflows used to mean weeks of manual setup, integration by integration, edge case by edge case. Increasingly, that first-draft build work can be directed rather than done by hand: AI agents can generate workflow configurations, draft integration mappings, and produce the initial pass on a customer's setup.

The job shifts with it. Instead of building every workflow yourself, you specify exactly what needs to exist, direct AI to build it, and apply the judgment AI can't: is this the right configuration for this customer's approval policy, will Legal and Finance actually sign off on it, does it hold up once real spend starts flowing through it. In practice, that might mean catching that the approval chain AI just drafted works perfectly for HQ, but misses a regional delegation-of-authority rule that would fail an audit in the customer's APAC entity.

As Omnea's AI Solutions Lead, you own deployment of the Omnea platform end to end - typically running 3-5 enterprise deployments concurrently - for some of Europe's most recognisable companies. You advise customers on the best-fit configuration, direct AI-assisted build work to get there fast, and validate every output against what the customer actually needs. You'll also deal with the politics that come with every enterprise rollout: the Legal team wanting one more sign-off, the Finance stakeholder who doesn't trust the new approval flow, the exec sponsor who's gone quiet. You become the internal voice of the customer, and you're judged on outcomes you can point to: time to launch, post-go-live CSAT, and whether that customer becomes a case study or reference.

This is an early hire on Omnea's customer team, working directly with our sales, customer, product, and engineering leadership. The future shape of the role is yours to define!

What You'll Do

Discover and design

  • Run discovery with customer stakeholders across Procurement, Finance, Legal, and IT, and translate their process into an Omnea configuration

  • Design the target workflow: approval chains, routing logic, integrations, and the edge cases that make procurement hard

  • On a deployment with a dozen-plus integrations, you own the sequencing - what has to land first, what blocks what - and the harder calls underneath it: which system is the source of truth for a given entity, and how records reconcile when two systems key that entity differently

  • Define success criteria and a realistic path to go-live with the customer's project sponsor

Build with AI, not instead of it

  • You're not just directing AI to draft your own deliverables faster - you're configuring the specialized agents Omnea's customers rely on every day: an intake agent that knows how to ask a procurement analyst the right follow-up question, a risk agent that flags what actually matters to this customer's Legal team

  • The real leverage comes from chaining agents together - an intake agent that hands clean, structured requests to a risk agent, which in turn routes into approvals with the right context already attached. You design how those agents work as a system, not just individually

  • Writing a spec for one agent is a skill. Writing one that holds up across a chain of agents - where one agent's output becomes another's input - is the actual bar here

  • Validate every AI-generated output against the customer's actual process, policy, and edge cases before anything ships

  • Handle what AI can't: judgment calls on ambiguous requirements, custom logic, and anything that needs a human read on internal politics

Deploy and prove value

  • Present configured workflows to stakeholders, from procurement analysts to CFOs, working through the pushback and internal politics that come with any enterprise rollout, and win their buy-in

  • Run multi-day onsite workshops with customers, coordinating dozens of stakeholders across multiple workstreams at once - a different muscle than a single stakeholder meeting

  • Project-manage the deployment: timelines, blockers, stakeholder alignment, and a clear path to launch, acting as an extension of the customer's team

  • Track adoption after go-live and keep the configuration working as the customer's process evolves

  • Work with Product and Engineering during the design phase, not just after something breaks in the field - you're often the earliest signal on whether a new module will hold up for an enterprise customer, and that shapes what gets built next

What's Different About This Role

  • You'll spend more time specifying and validating than building from scratch. AI produces the first draft; you make sure it's right for this customer

  • Writing instructions AI can act on precisely is a skill you'll build fast here. Vague requests produce vague configurations

  • Judgment matters more, not less. AI speeds up the build, but you decide whether the output is right for this contract, this Board, this customer

  • You'll keep experimenting as our AI tooling evolves, and share what works with the rest of the team

About You

We don't expect you to know how to do all of this on day one. TL;DR: you're ambitious and hard-working, as comfortable directing an AI agent through a tricky configuration as you are presenting a project plan to an exec. You make up for any gap in experience with hunger and a genuine growth mindset. You derive energy from building relationships, shipping projects, and making customers succeed.

  • 4-8 years in a fast-paced, high-bar environment: a startup, scale-up, consulting, banking, or something you built yourself

    • Less experience? Check out our Solutions Associate role

  • Comfortable directing AI tools to produce first-draft work, and confident enough in your own judgment to catch what's wrong. Prior use of tools like ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor is a strong plus. What matters most is your ability to write clear, specific instructions and evaluate what comes back

  • Client-facing experience, or the natural gravitas to be excellent at it. You can point to a time you went well beyond what a client expected

  • A track record of doing something exceptionally well, whether that's work, academia, sport, or anything else you've put your mind to

  • Comfortable reasoning about system architecture - how data models, primary keys, and integration sequencing interact across a dozen enterprise systems. You don't need to write the integration code, but you need to know why it breaks and be able to reason with the people who do, and you'll need to become an Omnea product expert

  • You build real relationships with people at any level, from a junior procurement analyst to a CFO, and know how to handle pushback and stakeholder politics, not just build rapport

  • Comfortable running rooms of stakeholders across a genuinely cross-functional tool - on a single project you'll interface with the CPO, Legal, Finance, AP, InfoSec, and Compliance, plus each of their technical resources, often all with competing priorities on the same decision

  • Comfortable moving between the detail and the big picture: configuring a workflow in the morning, presenting a project plan to an exec in the afternoon

  • Entrepreneurial, have high ownership, and want to be part of building something. We've signed up to the Future Founder Promise

  • An excellent communicator: clear and concise, verbal and written, even when the subject is complicated

  • Highly organised: comfortable running 3-5 enterprise deployments concurrently, each at a different stage, without dropping any of them

At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't quite match the full job spec! And regardless of your race, religion, colour, gender, or anything else! If you think you could be a good fit for Omnea, please reach out.

A few things to note:

  • We offer competitive geo-localised benefits, and you can check out our UK Benefits Package here and our US Benefits Package here.

  • We work Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays in-person at our offices. At this early stage of our company life-cycle it's important to us that we get this together-time, and you can read more about why we believe this is a winning move here

  • We're commercial, ambitious and we don't pretend otherwise! We're actively seeking folks looking to make the most of a career-defining opportunity, with the hunger to be part of building something really impressive. You can see our values here and our Omnea Future Founder's fund here!

  • We sometimes use AI note-takers to help us transcribe interview notes, so we can be more present in your interview. If you'd like to opt out of us using automatic transcribers, please note this in the free text field in your application, otherwise we'll take your application as confirmation that you're happy for us to use notetakers (whether added to video calls or in the background).

We are proud to be recognised for both our culture and product, and we are just getting started. Join us as we grow!

What We're Looking For

You'll work across every product team. You'll own the design system, own the front-end architecture, and set the standard for how we build interfaces. We're a tight-knit group of ambitious builders who hold the bar high. It took over 10,000 interviews to hire our first 50 Omneans. Over the next year, our engineering team will double in size, our enterprise customer base will grow from ~180 to 300+, and revenue will triple. The front end has to scale with it.

This is a craft role with real leverage. Almost every engineer at Omnea ships front end. What you build determines how well they do it.

Procurement is a harder interface problem than it sounds. Approval workflows that branch and re-route, dense tables people live in all day, intake forms that adapt to what someone is buying. Getting this right is the difference between software people tolerate and software people actually like using.

What Can You Expect On Our Engineering Team?

  • Join a Skilled Team. Become part of one of Europe's fastest-growing software companies, working alongside experienced full-stack product engineers and product designers from top technology businesses and startups.

  • Own the Design System. You'll own our design system outright: components, patterns, tokens, documentation, and adoption. You'll partner closely with Design to turn intent into reusable, high-quality primitives.

  • Own the Front-End Architecture. Deployment strategy, performance, build tooling, and the conventions everyone else follows. You'll set the direction rather than inherit it, working alongside the engineers and designers closest to each surface rather than owning it in isolation.

  • Leverage Across Every Team. You'll work with all of our engineering teams on their most front-end-heavy projects. The work you do multiplies across the whole org.

  • A Real Design Partnership. Every cross-functional team at Omnea has a dedicated Product Manager and Product Designer. You'll be the connective tissue between design intent and what actually ships, and the person designers come to when they want to know what's possible.

  • Work with Modern Technology. TypeScript everywhere, React and Next.js on the front end, and Meticulous for automated visual regression testing, so you can refactor the design system without fear. Behind it sits Postgres and AWS serverless infrastructure (Lambda, DynamoDB, and EventBridge), managed through Pulumi and deployed via GitHub Actions, with Datadog for observability.

  • AI-Native Development. AI is core to how we build. Engineers use Claude Code and agentic workflows every day to write, review, and ship code faster, and our product is itself built on AI agents that automate complex procurement workflows.

  • Continuous Delivery. We deploy small, incremental changes to production multiple times per day, enabling rapid iteration and fast customer feedback loops.

  • Collaboration and Autonomy. We operate as a high-trust team where individuals are expected to take ownership while collaborating closely to solve difficult problems.

  • Customers at the Center. We regularly engage directly with customers to understand their problems, gather feedback, and ensure we're building products that create genuine value.


About You

  • You're deep in React. You've built complex, production React applications and you understand the framework properly, not just the API surface. Rendering behaviour, state, performance, and where things break at scale.

  • You've owned front-end infrastructure. Rendering strategies, build tooling, bundle performance, and the architectural decisions underneath a large application.

  • You've built or owned a design system. Not just consumed one. You've made the calls on component APIs, driven adoption across teams, and dealt with the messy reality of migration and versioning.

  • You have taste. You care how things look and feel, you notice when something is only 90% right, and you can hold a genuine conversation with designers rather than just implementing tickets.

  • You know CSS deeply. Layout, styling architecture, and building interfaces that hold up across breakpoints, themes, and edge cases. You treat accessibility and motion as part of the craft rather than a checklist at the end.

  • You're a strong engineer first. Your depth and your interest sit in the front end, and that's the point of this role. But you're fluent in TypeScript generally and comfortable working beyond the browser when a problem calls for it.

  • You're motivated by impact. You care about what your work actually achieves, not just how it's built. You thrive with the autonomy to make meaningful decisions and take real ownership of outcomes.

  • You're a team builder. You're excited by maximising team performance, whether that means learning from others or taking the time to explain, give feedback, and level up those around you.

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. This role is new. Its shape will be partly yours to define, and you're happy tackling problems without a predefined solution, backed by an experienced team.


Nice-to-Haves

  • You've worked at design-led companies or somewhere with a genuinely high bar for interface quality.

  • You've performed exceptionally at something else, be it academics, sport, or work. You've gone above and beyond the norm.

  • You love engineering. It's more than a job. You've contributed to open source or worked on side projects just because you enjoy it.


Interview Process

Before applying, we strongly encourage you to spend a few minutes in our R&D Candidate Hub. It covers our engineering culture, ways of working, interview process, tech environment, and what it's like to build at Omnea.

>> R&D Candidate Hub: https://omnea.notion.site/R-D-Candidate-Hub-2f688cce658780f1b942c81cd3a032d4

data.description:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

"At TRM, we believe the people we hire will determine how far and how fast we can go in our mission to build a safer world for billions of people. That’s why we’re building a Talent team that sees recruiting as a craft and a competitive advantage, people who challenge assumptions, move with urgency, and are energized by building exceptional teams to solve incredibly hard problems. If that sounds like you, we’d love to meet you."

– Alicia Strait, VP of Talent, TRM Labs

As TRM expands across EMEA and other global markets, our ability to hire the right sellers, compliance experts, and go-to-market talent in-region determines how fast our blockchain intelligence reaches the institutions and agencies fighting illicit finance worldwide. As an International Sales Recruiter, you'll own high-priority searches across EMEA and beyond — Sales, Post-Sales, Compliance, Marketing, and broader business roles — partnering closely with hiring managers and Talent leadership to define strategy, map regional markets, engage passive candidates, and drive high-quality hiring decisions with speed and precision.

Your success is measured by the quality, velocity, and business impact of the hires you make across TRM's international business functions.

The impact you'll have:

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for international roles across Sales, Post-Sales, Compliance, Marketing, and other functions.

  • Act as a strategic talent partner to hiring managers, including advising on market dynamics, candidate calibration, sourcing strategy, and close approach.

  • Build and execute targeted sourcing strategies that identify, engage, and close exceptional talent across EMEA and other global markets.

  • Develop regional talent maps across priority markets that include high-performing companies, competitive talent, referral networks, and specialized candidate communities.

  • Create an exceptional candidate experience where every touchpoint reflects TRM's talent bar, mission, and operating principles.

  • Use data, market insight, and funnel conversion metrics to diagnose search health, influence hiring teams, and adjust strategy in real time.

  • Drive urgency and decision quality through clear calibration, structured feedback, and timely hiring decisions.

  • Continuously improve international recruiting including intake quality, scorecard alignment, sourcing strategy, debrief rigor, and offer execution.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Talent, People, Finance, Legal, and business leaders to navigate international hiring considerations and keep searches moving.

What we're looking for:

  • 7+ years of recruiting experience, with strong experience supporting international sales hiring in high-growth technology companies.

  • Proven success hiring across Sales, Post-Sales, Compliance, Marketing, and other business functions.

  • Strong knowledge of EMEA talent markets, with the ability to adapt strategy by region, function, and candidate profile.

  • Strong search fundamentals including market mapping, talent intelligence, passive candidate engagement, candidate assessment, and closing.

  • The ability to quickly understand complex business roles across GTM, compliance, marketing, and operations.

  • Strong analytical ability to interpret recruiting metrics, funnel health, conversion rates, and pipeline quality and translate them into action.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management that includes building trust, influencing hiring managers, pushing back thoughtfully, and operating as a strategic advisor.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including synthesizing market insight, candidate tradeoffs, and search progress clearly for stakeholders.

  • High ownership, autonomy, persistence, and judgment in navigating ambiguous, specialized, business-critical searches.

  • The ability to operate effectively in a remote, globally distributed environment with strong overlap across EMEA and U.S. business hours.

About the team:

  • Our talent team is fully remote and async-first. We keep work moving across time zones through Slack, thorough documentation, and proactive updates.

  • We stay tightly aligned through weekly hiring syncs, team sourcing syncs, and bi-weekly team meetings where we solve challenges together.

  • We care deeply about our craft: we continuously refine best practices and data quality to deliver an exceptional experience for candidates and internal stakeholders alike, backed by precise, reliable reporting.

  • We're globally distributed but most of us overlap between 7am–12pm PST for real-time collaboration.

  • Every team member, wherever they're based, maintains at least a 4-hour overlap with PST business hours.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within 72 hours of a role opening, you've scheduled the intake, researched and published the role, and brought 5 calibration profiles to the intake for the hiring manager to review.

  • Within a week of opening the role, you've mapped the total addressable market, built a shortlist of the top 30 profiles, conducted 5–10 recruiter screens, and stood up the full interview process — including the approved questions that define what good looks like on a recruiter screen.

  • Two weeks after the initial interviews, you analyze the data to identify what is and isn't driving pass rates and conversions, share insights and recommendations with the hiring team, and continue to monitor and adjust until the position is filled.

Our Onboarding Process:

  • Within your first 30 days, you’ll be fully onboarded, calibrated, and operating as the DRI for your positions.

  • Within your first 60 days, you’ll have your first sourced candidates reaching final rounds.

  • Within your first 90 days, you’ll have made 2–3 hires.

The following represents the estimated range of compensation for this role:

  • Individual pay is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. The compensation details listed in this posting reflect the US base salary only

  • The estimated base salary range for this role is $153,000 - $172,000.

  • Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

  • Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

Meet Siena

Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.

The team

We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.

We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.

If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.

The Role

You own the commercial relationship for Siena's highest-value brands: renewals, expansion, executive trust, and knowing your accounts better than anyone. A deployment strategist owns product outcomes for the same accounts, and together you're the Siena pod.

You're accountable for net dollar retention, expansion quota attainment, and executive relationship health across your book. You own our Growth and Strategic segment accounts, not the full customer book, working at the intersection of customer, sales, and your deployment strategist. Who You Are

Strong Signal: Not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one.

  • Hands-on AI experience: you've built an agent, automated a workflow, or created a tool, not just used ChatGPT for email

  • Close collaboration experience with product and engineering teams

  • Self-directed: brings solutions, not just problems

Nice to Have: Bonus, not required.

  • Experience at a native AI technology company

  • Comfort with API integrations, conversation flow design, and business intelligence tools

Not a Fit If:

  • You want a fixed playbook and clear SOPs before you start

  • You'd rather support the commercial conversation than own it

  • You need close oversight rather than working independently with your deployment strategist as your main partner

Why Siena?

Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.

Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.

A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.

A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.

Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build.

Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we.

AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.

Our values

The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback - both giving and receiving it - because they care more about getting things right than being polite.

They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward.

Our approach to AI

The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.

Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows.

At Siena, we're not just looking for people who can do a job. We're looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that's you, we look forward to your application.

About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About the Role

You’ll join our Research Team in London as a 3D Reconstruction Research Scientist/Engineer — working at both ends of the pipeline, from cutting-edge academic research to shipping directly to customers. What You’ll Bring

We're hiring a VP of Financial Planning & Analysis to build and lead our FP&A function. The company has recently raised significant funding, and it needs a hands-on leader to turn that strategy into agreed company targets, realistic budgets, clear spending priorities, and reporting leadership can rely on. You will build the financial model from scratch, set up the planning process, and give the CFO and executive team the numbers and recommendations they need to make decisions. The aim is for the CFO to spend their time on strategic finance, investors, and executive decisions, and less on building models, chasing inputs, or correcting reports.

This role will report to CFO. Over the first six months you will establish the function, and over the following year you will scale it, starting by building a small team and adding people as workload and data quality justify it. You will work closely with Accounting, Controlling, Treasury, Sales, Product, Engineering, Manufacturing, and People. The environment is demanding and not yet fully structured, so you need to be comfortable setting up processes from a blank page, working with incomplete data, and being questioned on your assumptions by the board and investors.

What you will do

  • Build the integrated financial model, including assumptions, scenarios, documentation, and ongoing maintenance, connecting pipeline, sales capacity, hiring, production, revenue timing, margins, investment, and cash. Keep the model clean and traceable, with clear units, periods, and reconciliation checks, and be able to explain and change it live.

  • Work with the CFO and CEO to turn company strategy into financial targets, then translate those targets into annual budgets, monthly forecasts, and quarterly reviews. Agree targets before departmental budgets are built, so every budget has a clear basis.

  • Run the planning process end to end: templates, submission deadlines, challenge sessions, consolidation, version control, and a repeatable forecasting calendar with named budget owners.

  • Deliver monthly management and board reporting that is reconciled to actuals, explained against budget and forecast, and includes cash implications, risks, and recommendations. Be clear about which figures are final, provisional, or missing, and keep a record of open data issues.

  • Agree a clear handover of actuals with Accounting and Controlling, including required inputs, reconciliation checks, delivery dates, and escalation routes.

  • Analyse product, contract, and customer economics with Manufacturing, Product, and Accounting. This covers unit production costs, gross margin, cohort performance, and the drivers of margin differences, separating proven costs from estimates and agreeing owners for missing data.

  • Link sales forecasts to signed contracts, delivery milestones, recognised revenue, and customer receipts. Keep committed forecasts distinct from closed contracts, and explain changes in amount, stage, timing, and probability. Make the impact of government procurement timing and hardware and software delivery risks explicit.

  • Track approved budgets against actual and committed spending, remaining funds, and projected overruns. Review hiring and investment cases to make sure the full cost is captured, including first-year cash and ongoing annual cost, with no omissions or double counting.

  • Work with Treasury to maintain a rolling short-term cash forecast and runway view, including customer receipts, payroll, suppliers, taxes, restricted cash, and entity funding needs.

  • Turn differences from plan into clear recommendations on what to fund, defer, reduce, or stop. Maintain a decision log and consolidated approval papers showing the decision needed, options, recommendation, approver, deadline, and the work that is blocked.

  • Review spending ratios and cost trends each quarter, investigate unusual movements with budget owners, and recommend actions with owners and dates, respecting that budget owners remain accountable for their own spend.

  • Prepare board and investor financial content within the authority agreed with the CFO, and keep the model and supporting evidence ready for future financing or due diligence when the CFO calls for it.

  • Hire, onboard, and develop a small FP&A team across locations. Set priorities, review quality, hold regular 1:1s, and build managers who resolve routine questions within FP&A without escalating to the CFO.

What we're looking for

  • Hands-on financial modelling: you have personally built a model from scratch that stood up to investor scrutiny, and you can explain and test every assumption without preparation. You delegate components while keeping ownership of the model logic and final quality.

  • Budgeting and funding experience: you have led, or worked directly under the accountable lead on, the financial work for a major funding round, and have turned the resulting strategy into targets, budgets, and corrective action. You can defend assumptions with boards and investors and maintain due-diligence evidence.

  • Strong judgment on prioritization and decisions: you focus on the decisions, deadlines, and cash risks that matter most, and get decisions made through concise options, recommendations, owners, and dates. You make a CFO's workload lighter rather than adding another review layer.

  • Business and spending judgment: you can challenge budgets constructively, expose omitted or duplicated costs, and tell healthy growth investment apart from structural margin or cash problems.

  • Reporting discipline: you use reconciled figures, documented definitions, and controlled assumptions, and you make data quality and cross-team dependencies visible. You set owners, deadlines, and follow-through without adding unnecessary bureaucracy.

  • Commercial understanding of manufacturing, government or defence procurement, deployment costs, and multi-currency operations.

  • People leadership: you have managed analysts, reviewed their work, set priorities, and developed independent owners, and you address weak output through coaching and accountability.

H Company is a next-generation AI research and product company pioneering the future of autonomous, agentic AI. Founded to build intelligence that acts, H Company is creating the foundational infrastructure for autonomous AI systems that drive real-world outcomes across industries.

The Role

Today, H is known for its story: its founders, its funding rounds, its press. We want it to be known for its value. Content is how that shift happens, one piece at a time: the case study a CIO forwards to their COO, the white paper a board reads before a steering committee, the article an engineer shares because it is precise.

You will be our first Content Manager and reporting to the head of marketing. You'll own the global content strategy and production, hands in hands with the brand, lead gen and product marketing stakeholders, from thought leadership to customer proof.

Our brand stance is that of a pragmatic visionary: bold on vision, precise and evidence-led on capability. You'll write and edit in both registers, a bold "vision voice" and a precise "capability voice", so that every piece speaks the language of the boardroom and holds up to the scrutiny of a CTO/builder.

You'll work hand in hand with Product Marketing, Growth, Research, Sales, our FDE teams and Communications, and with our external agencies and freelancers.

Build the content engine (Foundations)

Brands like Macy's, Decathlon, Carrefour, Asos, and Airbus Helicopters use Mirakl to grow their businesses in new and remarkable ways.

For more information: www.mirakl.com.

Mirakl in Numbers:

  • 🗓️ Founded in 2012 | Member of French Tech Next40
  • 👥 750+ employees in 9 offices worldwide: Paris, Barcelona, Bordeaux, Boston, London, Munich, New York, Sydney, Tokyo
  • 🇫🇷 350+ Mirakl Tech teams members mainly based in France

Working at Mirakl means accelerating your career alongside ambitious, passionate, and supportive colleagues. We're proud of the diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences that make our teams unique.

  • 💡 Work Hard Together: Teamwork and collaboration are the foundation of our success
